Same as MSPDI Tasks, except that Task.parentTaskUid and Task.siblingOrder give the WBS tree. GRS makes ID, OutlineLevel, OutlineNumber and Summary from that tree each time GRS writes MSPDI.

The task groups; GRS shows each one as one row in the Task Group Panel and as one Task Group Lane. taskGroupMembers says which tasks each task group holds. On reading an MSPDI file, GRS makes the task groups from the WBS.

type: object; title "How the schedule is drawn when opened"
text: How GRS draws the Schedule Document on opening. GRS always writes the keys that always have a value.

Display scale of the drawing in the Schedule Canvas, in percent: at 100 GRS draws every ...Px value as that many CSS pixels, at 50 at half size. This value scales shapes and text together and does not change the App Header, the Command Palette or the browser zoom.

Text size step of the Schedule Canvas: small, medium or large, which are 7.5, 8.75 and 10 CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100. The Schedule Document opens at this step; a reader who changes the step edits the Schedule Document.

How deep task groups with treeState auto open. A top-level task group is depth 1. With value N, task groups down to depth N are open, so GRS shows rows down to depth N + 1; 0 shows only the top-level task groups, closed.
Where the View starts when the Schedule Document opens: notDecided lets GRS choose, placed gives the day at the left edge and the task group at the top edge.
notDecided: no person has chosen a place yet, and GRS chooses one when GRS opens the Schedule Document; placed: the other keys give the place.
The day at the left edge of the View.
Where the left edge falls inside leftEdgeDay, as a part of that day; 0 is the start of the day.
The task group at the top edge of the View. When that task group no longer exists, scrollPosition becomes notDecided.
Where the top edge falls inside that task group, as a part of the step of the task group (the height of the Task Group Lane plus the gap below), not in pixels; 0 is the top of the Task Group Lane.
The first day of the fit span (included), in the time zone that GRS shows the Schedule Canvas in (viewTimeZone).
The last day of the fit span; the fit span includes the column of that day.
The time zone that the Time Ruler and the shown date-times use: sameAsScheduleData follows project.scheduleDataTimeZone, fixed uses the offset given here.
sameAsScheduleData: show the Schedule Data time zone, and follow the Schedule Data time zone when that time zone changes; fixed: show the offset given here.
The UTC offset that GRS shows the Schedule Canvas in.
Up to four extra clocks. While GRS shows the time of day, GRS shows each extra clock as one more row under the Time Ruler.
The UTC offset of this extra clock.
Whether this clock is the standard-time or the daylight-time zone of the offset of this clock. This value picks the zone name that GRS shows; GRS uses the offset itself all year.
Whether GRS shows the time of day on the Schedule Canvas; the stored date-times keep their time either way. A new Schedule Document starts with false.
Whether GRS shows Plan Bars, apart from isActualVisible. A new Schedule Document starts with true.
Whether GRS shows Actual Bars, apart from isPlanVisible. A new Schedule Document starts with true.
Whether GRS draws the earlier plan (baselineTasks) over the current tasks. A new Schedule Document starts with false.

up stacks the tasks of a task group so that the tasks climb to a goal at the upper right; down stacks them so that the tasks descend to a goal at the lower right. A new Schedule Document starts with up.
Whether the theme is monochrome. A new Schedule Document starts with false.
Width of the Task Group Panel, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100.
Whether the number taskGroupPanelWidthPx, instead of a drag of the Panel Divider, sets the width of the Task Group Panel. A new Schedule Document starts with false.
The state of the head of the Task Group Panel (level 0), above all top-level task groups. collapsed draws no task group at all. A new Schedule Document starts with auto.
The Pinned Task Groups: task groups that stay together at the top of the Task Group Lanes, to compare them with task groups far away. Absent means no pinned task group.

Same as MSPDI Project.
Same as MSPDI Project/UID. Before saving over a GRS JSON or MSPDI file, GRS checks this value, project.name and the file name to tell whether the file holds the same Schedule Document.

Same as MSPDI Project/CalendarUID. GRS counts all working days with this one calendar. If this value is absent or names no calendar, GRS uses the calendar with isBaseCalendar true and the smallest ordinal, else a built-in default.

Same as MSPDI Project/Name. GRS does not show the Project Name (GRS shows title as the Project Title). GRS uses the Project Name only to tell whether a GRS JSON or MSPDI file GRS is about to overwrite holds the same Schedule Document.
Same as MSPDI Project/Title. GRS shows the value as the Project Title in the App Header and uses the value as the default file name in the Save As Dialog. When absent, the browser tab shows Untitled.
Same as MSPDI Project/Subject.
Same as MSPDI Project/Category.
Same as MSPDI Project/Company.
Same as MSPDI Project/Manager.
Same as MSPDI Project/Author. The author is not who wrote the Schedule Document last (documentStamp.lastEditedBy).
Same as MSPDI Project/Revision. The revision is not one of the documentStamp times.
Same as MSPDI Project/CreationDate. GRS writes the value when GRS makes a new Schedule Document.
Same as MSPDI Project/StartDate.
The fixed UTC offset of the clock of the Schedule Data date-times, for example UTC+09:00. The offset is standard time, with no daylight saving. GRS does not write the offset to MSPDI.

Same as MSPDI Project/MinutesPerDay: the length of one working day (1d) in minutes, {{S-128}} when absent. GRS warns on opening the Schedule Document if the working times of any working day add up to a total other than this value.
Same as MSPDI Project/MinutesPerWeek.
Same as MSPDI Project/DaysPerMonth.
Same as MSPDI Project/WeekStartDay, where 0 is Sunday. Absent means Monday (1).

Same as MSPDI Project/DefaultStartTime: the time of day GRS gives a start that has a date and no time (the start of a Task or a BaselineTask, actualStart, resume, project.startDate); {{S-482}} when absent. A milestone's start gets defaultFinishTime instead.

Same as MSPDI Project/DefaultFinishTime: the time of day GRS gives a finish that has a date and no time (the finish of a Task or a BaselineTask, actualFinish, stop, deadline, project.statusDate); {{S-483}} when absent. A milestone's start gets this time as well.
The hue of the theme, in degrees. Every color written as {"kind":"theme"} uses this hue. A new Schedule Document starts with 214.

How many working days the progress point of a parent task may lie outside the progress points of the work below the parent task, before Delay Diagnostics asks whether an update is missing. A new Schedule Document starts with 1.
One counter for the uids of tasks, resources, assignments and calendars. GRS never reuses a uid, so a new uid is always above this value.
How many times GRS has imported an MSPDI file into this Schedule Document; 0 means never. GRS compares TaskOrigin.lastSeenImportNumber with this number.
The OutlineLevel at which the tasks of an imported MSPDI file start (not counting the project summary task); export writes from this number. A new Schedule Document starts with 1.

The format the Schedule Document came from: grs for a Schedule Document made in GRS, pj12 or pj15 for an MSPDI file (pj15 when the file has any element that only pj15 has). GRS does not write this value to MSPDI.

The order of this span within the day; GRS writes the spans in the order of their start.

Same as MSPDI Task. GRS reads the progress state with these checks, first match wins: no actualStart, not started; actualFinish set, finished; resumeValid false, suspended with no resume date; resume set, suspended with a resume date; otherwise in progress.
Same as MSPDI Task/UID.

text: The parent task in the WBS. Absent means a top-level task.

The order of this task among the tasks under the same parent task.
Same as MSPDI Task/Name.
Same as MSPDI Task/Notes.
Same as MSPDI Task/Start. GRS does not open a GRS JSON or MSPDI file in which a task has no start.
Same as MSPDI Task/Finish. GRS does not open a GRS JSON or MSPDI file in which a task has no finish.
Same as MSPDI Task/Milestone. Absent reads as false. When true, TaskVisual holds milestoneShape; otherwise TaskVisual holds taskShape.
Same as MSPDI Task/Deadline.
Same as MSPDI Task/ActualStart. Absent means the task is not started.
Same as MSPDI Task/Stop: the end of the actual work so far on a task that is in progress or suspended. On a finished task actualFinish holds that end; GRS empties stop when GRS finishes a task.
Same as MSPDI Task/ActualFinish. Present only on a finished task; a percentComplete of 100 does not mean finished.
Same as MSPDI Task/Resume: on a suspended task, the planned restart of the remaining work.
Same as MSPDI Task/ResumeValid. On a task with actualStart and no actualFinish, false means suspended with no resume date, and GRS does not use a date in resume.

Same as MSPDI Task/PercentComplete, except that GRS recalculates the value as actual working time (actualStart to actualFinish, or to stop) over planned working time (start to finish), times 100, rounded, with no cap at 100. With no planned working time, as on a milestone, the value is 100 once actualFinish is present, else 0.
